argument_summary: The audited claim should be narrowed. We are not defending unconditional certification on the present record. We are defending a certification basis that relies on the admissible evidence showing aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents, while expressly treating the current mortgage servicing regression as a material limitation that must be included in the current-release certification documentation before launch. On that reading, the prior approval and informal monitoring note remain contextual only, and the packet can be handled as a caveated certification record rather than an escalation case.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is not necessary if the issue is framed as a documentation predicate inside the certification packet rather than as a contradiction of the certification direction itself. The admissible record already supports overall readiness and identifies the exact limitation that must be carried into current-release documentation. Treating this as a bounded caveat preserves launch velocity better than reopening the decision on the basis of contextual evidence that no one is claiming is sufficient by itself.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy is explicit: current release documentation must reflect current evaluation results, and material segment weaknesses must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved mitigation. The admissible evidence does not support using the prior model-family approval or the release-thread monitoring comment as substitutes for that predicate. Our position is therefore narrower: certification is supportable only if the audit packet is understood as current-release certification with explicit disclosure of the mortgage servicing weakness as part of the certification basis, not as clean compliance already proven by stale approval.
concessions: The present record does not prove that the current release documentation has already been updated to disclose the mortgage servicing weakness.
The prior approval predates the retrieval configuration change and current evaluation batch, so it cannot satisfy the current-release documentation requirement.
The informal monitoring comment is not reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language.
